body.translated_text: Now begins the <s>Sāṃkhyatattvapradīpa</s> (Light on the Principles of Sāṃkhya).

children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and the pure <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness), this
<s>Pradīpa</s> (Light) on the principles of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> is composed by me for the benefit of others.

body.text: iha khalu pravāhavidhvastottaraṇopāyā iva sāṃkhyatantrādhyayanapariśramālasāstatprakriyājñānatarīvihīnāḥ śabdodadhāvananyāvalambanāḥ sīdanti tattaraṇopāyaḥ sakalasāṃkhyaprakriyādyotako bahvartho 'lpākṣaro mayā prakāśyate / kāpilatantrādhyayanālasaistatprakriyājijñāsāyāmidameva prakaraṇaṃ samyagavalokanīyamatyugraśubhāśubhādṛṣṭaphalavat prayatnaṃ vinaiva sarvamatraivādhigantavyam ayatnalabdherthe yatnādarśanāt / uktaṃ ca sāṃkhyācāryaiḥ /

children.text: akke cenmadhu vindeta kimarthaṃ parvataṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: If one could find honey in an <s>arka</s> plant, why would one go to the mountain?
When the desired goal is accomplished, what wise person would exert effort?

body.translated_text: Indeed, here those who are weary from the labor of studying the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system, deprived of the boat of knowledge of its methodology — like those whose means of crossing have been destroyed by the current — having no other support in the ocean of words, sink. The means for crossing that, illuminating the entire <s>Sāṃkhya</s> methodology, rich in meaning yet brief in words, is set forth by me. By those weary from the study of the <s>Kāpila</s> (Sāṃkhya) system, in the desire to know its methodology, this very treatise alone should be carefully examined. Like the fruit of actions producing extremely intense auspicious or inauspicious unseen results, everything should be understood right here without effort, since effort is not seen to be required when the matter is obtainable without it. And it has been said by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers:

body.text:
ṛjumārgeṇa siddhyato 'rthasya vakreṇa sādhanāyogāt iti kecit /
  duḥkhatrayābhighātodvignacittāstānnivṛttyupāyameva tāvadabhikāmayante / taṃ cāgre darśayiṣyāmaḥ / duḥkhatrayaṃ ca ādhyātmikamādhibhautikamādhidaivikaṃ ca / tatrādhyātmikaṃ dvidhā śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ca vātapittaśleṣmaṇāṃ vaiṣamyanimittaṃ śārīram kāmakrodhalobhamoherṣyāviṣādaviṣayaviśeṣādarśanakāraṇakaṃ mānasam / āntaropāyasādhyatvādādhyātmikaṃ duḥkhamiti vyapadiśyate / brāhmopāyasādhyamapi duḥkhaṃ dvividham / ādhibhautikamādhidaivaikaṃ ca / tatrādhibhautikaṃ mānuṣapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvaranibandhanam / ādhidaivikaṃ pakṣarākṣavināyakagrahādyāveśanimittam / sarvaṃ mānasapratyakṣam / etad duḥkhaṃ rajaḥpariṇāmaviśeṣo nityapariṇāmitvādidamapi nityamiti na śakyate bādhitum tathāpi śakya eva tadabhibhavaḥ kartuṃ sādhanena tacca sādhanaṃ śāstrajanitaṃ prakṛtipuruṣānyatājñānaṃ nānyaditi tacchāstrapratipādyārthaścaturvidhaḥ tadyathā kaścidarthaḥ prakṛtireva na tu kasyacit vikṛtiryathā mūlaprakṛtiḥ sā sarvasya mūlamādikāraṇaṃ na tu tasyāḥ kāraṇāntaraṃ kiñcit pramāṇasiddhaṃ tathātve vā mūlakṣatikārītyanavasthā syāt svasyaiva svakāraṇatve tu tasyāpekṣayā kāraṇatvāt svasyaiva pūrvavartitvaṃ kāryatvāt paścādvartitvamityasaṃbhavaḥ / sakāraṇatve ajāmekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāmityajatvapratipādanaparaśrutivirodhaḥ syāt / sā ca prakarotīti prakṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ sattvarajastamasāṃ sāmyāvasthā /
  kaścidarthaḥ prakṛtirvikṛtiśca tacca mahattattvamahaṅkāraḥ pañcatanmātrāṇi ceti saptasaṅkhyāko gaṇaḥ kasyacitprakṛtiḥ kasyacidvikṛtiḥ / tadyathā mahattattvamahaṅkārasya prakṛtirvikṛtiśca mūlaprakṛteḥ tathā ahaṅkāraḥ pañcatanmātrāṇāmindriyāṇāṃ ca prakṛtirvikṛtirmahataḥ tathā pañcatanmātrāṇi bhūtānāmākāśādīnāṃ prakṛtayo vikṛtayaścāhaṅkārasya / pañca mahābhūtānyekādaśendriyāṇi ceti ṣoḍaśasaṅkhyāko gaṇo vikṛtireva na tu kasyacitprakṛtiḥ / nanu pṛthivyādīnāmapi goghaṭavṛkṣādayo vikārā upalabhyante tathā tadvikāraviśeṣāṇāṃ payobījādīnāṃ dadhyaṅkurādaya iti kathaṃ vikṛtitvameva teṣāmiti cenna tattvāntaropādānatvaṃ prakṛtitvamihābhyupagatam na tveteṣāṃ tadasti sthaulyendriyagrāhyatayā goghaṭādīnāṃ samānatvāt na tattvāntaratā pṛthivyādibhyaḥ / uktaṃ ca tattvakaumudyām "sarveṣāṃ goghaṭādīnāṃ sthūlatendriyagrāhyatā ca sameti" na tattvāntaram / puruṣastu na kasyacit prakṛtirapariṇāmitvānnāpi vikṛtirnityatvādanyathā sādhanasādhyābhivyaktiḥ syāt ghaṭavat /
  pramāṇavirahiṇo 'rthasya nṛśṛṅgasādṛśyābhyupagamāt / uktaprameyasādhakaṃ trividhaṃ pramāṇamurarīkatyam pratyakṣamanumānamāptavacanaṃ ceti / sāṅkhyācāryaiḥ / anyavādyaṅgīkṛtapramāṇānāmeteṣveva triṣvantarbhāvaḥ / uktaṃ ca 'sarvapramāṇasiddhatvāditi'; sarveṣāṃ vādyantarābhyupagatānāṃ pramāṇānāṃ siddhatvāt triṣvevāntarbhāvādityarthaḥ / nanu yatra yatra pratyakṣamapravartamānaṃ tattadatyantā 'saditi vyāptiḥ suprasiddhā śaśaśṛṅgakūrmalomādau evaṃ pradhānasyāpi pratyakṣāsiddhatvāt tadatyantāsattvameva yuktaṃ gaganakusumādīnāmiveti cenna nahi yat pratyakṣāgocaraṃ tadatyantāsaditi vyāptigraho yukto 'nyathā gṛhānnirgatasya gṛhadhanaputrapaśuvanitādīn sukhasādhanabhūtānapaśyatastannāśaniścayajaduḥkhavipluṣṭāntaḥkaraṇasya rudato maraṇaṃ syāt na tvevamasti / kiñca kiṃ sarvapratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ sattve hetuḥ kiñcitpratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ vā ? nādyaḥ nahi gṛhāntaradeśāntarakālāntaragataṃ vastu kenāpyayoginā pratyakṣeṇa viṣayīkartuṃ śakyamanyathā sarva eva sarvajñaḥ syāt parabuddherapratyakṣatayā sarvaiḥ sarvaṃ pratyakṣeṇa gṛhyate navetyasarvajñena niścetumaśakyatayā saṃśayānivṛtteḥ / nāpi caramaḥ vyabhicārāt nahi nagarasthena svenānupalabdho gavaya etāvataivāraṇyakopalabdhasya tasyāpalāpasambhavaḥ / uktañca līlāvatīkāreṇa "sarvādṛṣṭeśca sandehāt svādṛṣṭervyabhicārata" iti / tasmāt pratyakṣapravṛttipratikūlābhāvaviśiṣṭaṃ pratyakṣaṃ yatra na pravartate tadatyantāsaditi niścetuṃ śakyam na tu pratyakṣāpravṛttimātrāt anyathā puruṣapradhānamahatsvargāpūrvadevatādīnāmatīndriyāṇāmatyantābhāvaḥ syāt / tena viyati gacchataḥ patatriṇo grahaṇe 'tidūratvameva pratikūlam tathā netragatakajjalagrahaṇe 'tisāmīpyam evaṃ rūpaśabdādigrahaṇe āndhyabadhiratvādayaḥ tathā viṣayagrahaṇe manasaḥ kāmādyabhivyāptiḥ yathā kāmādyabhivyāptamanāḥ sphītālokamadhyavartinamindriyasannikṛṣṭamapyarthaṃ na paśyati / paramāṇvādiviṣayatāyāṃ saukṣmyameva pratikūlam yataḥ praṇihitamanā api taṃ na paśyati / bhittyādiparavastugrahaṇe tadvyavadhānameva pratikūlaṃ sampratipannapadārthagrahaṇe hastādivyavadhānavat / kvacidabhibhavaḥ yathā ahani saurībhirbhābhirabhibhūtaṃ nakṣatrasūryādigrahe cakṣuḥ samarthaṃ na bhavati / kvacit samānābhihāraḥ pratikūlaṃ yathā jalāśaye 'mbudavimuktajalabindugrahaṇe netrāsāmarthyam / kvacidanudbhavaḥ yathā kṣīradadhyādyavasthāyāṃ dadhighṛtādivivecanāsāmarthyam / evaṃ sati dṛḍhatarapramāṇāntaraprasiddhe vastuni pratyakṣāpravṛttāvetadanyatamaṃ pratibandhakaṃ kalpyate na tu tadabhāvādevāpravṛttiḥ / uktañca sāṅkhyamūlakāreṇa "saukṣmyāt tadanupalabdhirnābhāvāt" / nanu kvacitpratyakṣaprasiddhasya kvacitsandehādanumānaviṣayatā na tvasya tadastītyabhāva eva yukta iti cenna kāryaṃ hi kāraṇānumāpakaṃ bhavatīti sarvavādyabhimatam tathā ca mahadādikāryānyathānupapattyaiva pradhānasiddhiriti na tadabhāvo yuktaḥ / nanu kāryānyathānupapattyā kāraṇasiddhau tantrāntarābhimatakāraṇasiddhiḥ setsyati na tu tvadabhimatapradhānasiddhiriti cenna mataparyālocanena yanmataṃ kapilasūtranibaddhaṃ pradhānasādhanānuguṇaṃ tadeva yuktisahamanyat tu bāhyamatavat matābhāsatvādbādhyameva / tadyathā 'asataḥ sajjāyata'; iti bauddhamate pradhānasiddhiḥ 'sataḥ sajjāyata'; iti sāṅkhyamataviruddhatvānna paṇḍitamukhamaṇḍanāyālam sadasatoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvāsambhavāt asadalīkaṃ kāraṇaṃ sattvādirūpaśabdādyātmakaṃ kathaṃ syāt sadasatostādātmyadarśanāt kāryaṃ hi kāraṇasamavetaṃ tantupaṭādisthaleṣu prasiddham tathā ca ghaṭo 'san paṭo 'sannityasatsamavetaṃ sarvo vyavahartā vyavahareta na tu sadidamiti sattāvaiśiṣṭyena pratītiḥ syāt /
  atha sadvivarto 'yaṃ prapañca iti yadvedāntimatam / tadapyasādhu anenāpi sataḥ sajjāyata iti matasiddhirna syāt / advayasya sadvayatayā bhāne rajjoḥ srakkhaṇḍasarppādyātmanā bhānavat bhrāntireva syāt bādhitaviṣayatayā rajjusarpapratyayavat prapañcajñānasyāpramāṇatayā pramārūpaṃ jñānamevāstamiyāt / na ceṣṭāpattirguruśiṣyottarapraśnayorapramāṇabuddhyā vyavahāramātrocchedaḥ syāt laukikavaidikavyavahārānuṣṭhāne ca kasyacit pravṛttyanupapattyā bhogāpavargau na syātāmiti tacchāstrāprāmāṇyaṃ syāt / apasiddhāntaśca na hi vedāntimate brahma vivarti bhavati / uktañca -
  bālān prati vivarto 'yaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sakalaṃ jagat /
  avivartitamānandamāsthitāḥ kṛtinaḥ sadā // iti /
  sato 'sajjāyata iti sataḥ paramāṇorasaddvyaṇukākhyaṃ kāryaṃ jāyata iti kaṇabhakṣākṣacaraṇamatamapi na yuktisaham tathā hi paramāṇurhi dvyaṇukasamavāyikāraṇam dvyaṇukaṃ cāsadityasattvāviśeṣācchaśaśṛṅgādisamavāyikāraṇatāpi paramāṇau syāt sadasatoḥ samavāyāsambhavācca asatā tādātmye satopyasattvaṃ syāt nanvasattvaṃ nāma prāgabhāvapratiyogitvaṃ na tu vāyurūpādivat trikālāsattvamiti cenna kimidaṃ prāgabhāvapratiyogitvamasattvam kiṃ prāgabhāvapratiyogitvādasattvamasattvādvā prāgabhāvapratiyogitvam ? nādyaḥ sarveṣāṃ kāryapadārthānāmasattvāviśeṣeṇākāśapuṣpādiṣvivāsattvenaiva vyavahāraḥ syāt teṣāmapi prāgabhāvapratiyogitvāt tathā ca kāryapadārthagataguṇasāmānyādīnāmucchedaḥ syāt teṣāṃ bhāvadharmatvenāsattvenāvasthānāt / na ca kūrmalomāderasyāsato viśeṣaḥ sāmānyādyabhāvena bhedakadharmābhāvāt / nāpi caramaḥ asattvātprāgabhāvapratiyogitve naraśṛṅgādīnāmapi prāgabhāvapratiyogitvaṃ syāt prāgabhāvasya ca svapratiyogyutpādakatvaniyamena sarveṣāmasatāṃ sattvaṃ syāt sadasadvibhāgo jagati dattajalāñjaliḥ syāditi na tārkikavaiśeṣikamataṃ vicārasaham / tasmāt sataḥ sajjāyata iti sāṅkhyamatameva yuktisaham / sataḥ kāraṇāt svotpatteḥ prāgapi sadeva kāryaṃ kāraṇavyāpārādabhivyaktimāpnoti / na ca siddhasādhanatā kāraṇavaiyarthyaṃ ceti vācyam kāryasattve 'pi tadabhivyaktau kāraṇaṃ prayojanavaditi na kiñcidavadyam / asatkāryapakṣe tu kāraṇavaiyarthyaṃ sphuṭameva na hyasataḥ kāraṇasambandho nirūpayituṃ śakyate sambaddhameva asambaddhena janyate asambaddhasya janyatve sarvasmāt sarvaṃ syāt kāraṇaniyamo 'stamiyāt / asaccetkāryaṃ na kāraṇavyāpārāt sadbhavitumarhati uktañca tattvakaumudyām - nahi nīlaṃ śilpasahasreṇāpi pītaṃ kartuṃ śakyam / na ca kāraṇavyāpārāt pūrvaṃ ghaṭo 'san saṃśca vyāpārānantaramiti ghaṭasya sattvāsattve dharmāviti vācyam dharmasya bhāvadharmatvena tenaiva dharmiṇaḥ sattvaṃ svasthityanyathānupapattyā sādhitamiti sadeva kāryaṃ kāraṇavyāpārādūrdhvamiva prāgapi / kāraṇavyāpārastu tadabhivyaktāvananyathāsiddhaḥ anyatrāpi kāraṇavyāpārādabhivyaktireva dṛśyate yathā 'vaghātena dhānyeṣu taṇḍulānām avapīḍanena tileṣu tailasya dohanena saurabheyīṇāṃ payasa iti / asadutpattau tu na dṛṣṭānto 'sti tasmāt sadeva kāryaṃ kāraṇavyāpāreṇābhivyajyate / asatā kāraṇasambandhāsambhavāt na tasya tadutpādakatvam uktañca sāṅkhyācāryaiḥ
  asattvānnāsti sambandhaḥ kāraṇaiḥ sattvasaṅgibhiḥ //

body.translated_text: And for one who desires the origination of something unconnected [with its cause], there is no stable determination.

body.text: kiñca sambaddhamapi tadeva karoti yatra yat kāraṇaṃ śaktam śaktiśca kāryaikādhigamyā yathā cakṣuṣaiva rūpajñānaṃ bhavati nendriyāntareṇetīdameva tatra śaktamityadhigamyate / tathā ca sā śaktiḥ śaktakāraṇāśrayā śakyakāryāśrayā sarvatra vā syāt ? antye sarvasmāt sarvaṃ syāt / atha kārye sā śaktistadā kathamasataḥ kāryasya śaktyāśrayatā tathā ca śaktena śakyamutpādyate śakyaṃ ca kāraṇātmakam kāraṇaṃ ca saditi kathaṃ tadabhinnaṃ kāryamasatsyāt 'uktañca śaktasya śakyakaraṇāditi'; / upādānopādeyabhāvagrahaṇācca na bhedastantupaṭayoryayorbhedo na tayorupādānopādeyabhāvo yathāśvavṛkṣayoḥ / ito 'pi nārthāntaratvaṃ tantupaṭayoḥ saṃyogāprāptyadarśanāt arthāntaratve saṃyogo dṛṣṭo rajjughaṭakuṇḍabadarādau aprāptirapi dṛṣṭā sumeruvidhyayoriva iha ca saṃyogāprāptyorabhāvānna tantubhyo 'rthāntaraṃ paṭaḥ / kāryakāraṇayorabhedasādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ coktaṃ sāṅkhyācāryaiḥ tadyathā na paṭastantubhyo bhidyate taddharmatvāt iha yadyato bhidyate tat tasya dharmo na bhavati yathā gauraśvasya dharmaśca paṭastantūnāntasmānnārthāntaram / gurutvāntarāgrahaṇādapi na kāraṇādarthāntaraṃ kāryam / evamabhede siddhe tantava eva tena tena saṃsthānaviśeṣeṇa pariṇatāḥ paṭo na tu paṭastantubhyo 'rthāntaram / na cātmāśrayabuddhibhedādarthakriyābhedācca bhedasiddhiḥ kāryakāraṇayoriti vācyam ekasminnapi viśeṣāntarāvirbhāvatirobhāvābhyāmātmāśrayārthakriyābuddhibhedasambhavānna tadanyathānupapattyā bhedasiddhiḥ / tatra ekasyāpi kūrmasyāvayavā niḥsarantyāvirbhavanti ta eva kūrmaśarīre niviśamānāstirobhavanti nahi te kūrmāvayavā utpadyante dhvaṃsante vā evamekasyāpi suvarṇasya mṛdo va kaṭakakuṇḍalādayo ghaṭādayo niḥsaranta utpannā iti vyavahāraṃ bhajante ta eva niviśamānāstirobhavanti naśyantītyucyante na punaḥ sadasatornirodhotpādayornidarśanamasti / uktaṃ ca bhagavatā nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sata iti / yathā saṅkocavikāśavadbhyaḥ svāvayavebhyaḥ kūrmo na bhidyate tathā mṛtsuvarṇādibhyo 'pi kaṭakakuṇḍalādayo na bhinnāḥ / na ca nāma buddhyarthakriyābhedāt kāryakāraṇayorbhedasiddhiriti vācyam naṭe vyabhicārāt / naṭo hi daśaratho 'haṃ rāmo 'haṃ yudhiṣṭhiro 'hamiti svayamanantanāmā bhūtvā nāmāntareṇa veśāntaramarthakriyāntarañca kurute tathā ca satyapi bhedatraye naṭabhedādarśanāt yathāhuḥ -

children.translated_text: The form, the function,
and the name of the actor are known to be distinct;
yet the actor does not become different — why?
This must certainly be answered by the wise.

body.translated_text: Moreover, even that which is connected [with the cause] produces only that for which the cause is capable, and the capacity (<s>śakti</s>) is known only through the attainment of a single effect — just as visual cognition of form occurs only through the eye and not through another sense organ, and so it is ascertained that only this [eye] is capable of that. And so, does that capacity reside in the capable cause, or in the possible effect, or in both? If the last, then everything would arise from everything. But if the capacity resides in the effect, then how can there be a locus of capacity for an effect that is non-existent? And furthermore, the capable [cause] produces the possible [effect], and the possible [effect] is of the nature of the cause, and the cause exists — so how could the effect, which is non-different from the cause, be non-existent? As it has been said: 'Because the capable produces the possible.' And from the apprehension of the material-cause and product relationship, there is no difference between threads and cloth; for those between which there is difference, there is no material-cause and product relationship, as between a horse and a tree. Moreover, there is no otherness between threads and cloth, because neither conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) nor non-contact (<s>aprāpti</s>) is observed [between them]. In cases of otherness, conjunction is observed, as in the case of a rope, pot, water-vessel, and jujube fruit; non-contact is also observed, as between Mount <s>Meru</s> and a type of knowledge. And here, since there is absence of both conjunction and non-contact, cloth is not something other than threads. The proof establishing the non-difference of cause and effect has been stated by the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> masters as follows: cloth is not different from threads, because it possesses the properties of threads; for in this world, whatever is different from something does not possess the properties of that thing, just as a cow does not possess the properties of a horse; and cloth possesses the properties of threads — therefore it is not something different. Also, because no difference in weight is apprehended, the effect is not something other than the cause. Thus, non-difference having been established, the threads themselves, transformed into particular configurations, are the cloth — but the cloth is not something other than the threads. Nor should it be objected that the difference of cause and effect is established by the difference of self-referential cognition (<s>ātmāśraya</s>) and functional capacity (<s>arthakriyā</s>); for even in a single thing, through the appearance and disappearance of different particular features, there is the possibility of difference in self-referential cognition, functional capacity, and conceptual understanding — so the difference is not established by the absence of any other explanation. In this regard: even for a single tortoise, the limbs extend and appear, and those very same limbs, entering back into the tortoise's body, disappear. Indeed, those limbs of the tortoise are not [newly] produced or destroyed. Similarly, even for a single piece of gold or clay, the bracelets, earrings, and so forth, or the pots and so forth, come forth and are conventionally said to be 'produced'; those very same, entering back, disappear and are said to 'perish' — but there is no example of the actual destruction or production of what is real or unreal. And the Blessed One has said: 'The existent never comes to have non-being; the non-existent never comes to have being.' Just as the tortoise is not different from its own limbs that contract and expand, so too bracelets, earrings, and the like are not different from clay, gold, and so forth. Nor should it be said that difference of cause and effect is established by the difference of name, cognition, and functional capacity — because of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) in the case of the actor. For an actor, himself becoming one of endless names — 'I am <s>Daśaratha</s>,' 'I am <s>Rāma</s>,' 'I am <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>' — performs different costumes and different functions under different names. And thus, despite the threefold difference existing, since no actual difference of the actor is observed, as they say:

ekasyāpi vahnerdāhakatvapācakatvabhedena nānārthakriyākāritvaṃ dṛśyate na hyetāvatā vahnirbhedamadhigacchati ekaikasya tṛṇasyātapavṛṣṭyādinivṛttāvasāmarthye 'pi bahūni militvāvasthāviśeṣamavāpya yathā tānyeva tannivṛttau sāmarthyamadhigacchanti tathaika eva tantuḥ prāvaraṇādyarthakriyāsamartho 'pi militāsta evāvasthāviśeṣaṃ prāpyāvirbhūtapaṭabhāvāḥ prāvaraṇādyarthakriyāṃ kariṣyanti tasmātsadeva kāryaṃ kāraṇāt tadabhivyaktiriti / nanvāvirbhāvaḥ kāraṇavyāpārātpūrvaṃ sannasan vā ? ādye kāraṇavyāpārāsambavaḥ nahi sadutpattau kenāpi kāraṇāni vyāpāryante / antye prāptamasadutpādanatvamiti cenna tavāpi keyamutpattiḥ satyasatī vā ? ādye na kāraṇaprayojanaṃ paśyāmaḥ / antye 'sadutpattirutpadyata iti tadutpatterapyutpattyantaraṃ tatrāpyanyaditi sphuṭaivānavasthā / atha paṭāt tadutpattirnātiricyate tadā paṭa ityukte punarutpadyate iti na vācyaṃ paunaruktyāt tathotpadyate ityuktvā punaḥ paṭa iti na vācyaṃ pūrvoktadoṣādeva paṭo vinaśyatītyapi na vācyaṃ virodhāt tasmātsvasattāsamavāyo vā svakāraṇasamavāyo vā paṭotpattiḥ samavāyasya ca nityatvena sarvathāpi na paṭotpattiḥ sambhavati na tadarthañca kāraṇāni vyāpāryyante tathā ca sata eva paṭāderāvirbhāve kāraṇāpekṣeti na kiñcidavadyam / na ca paṭādikāryarūpeṇa kāraṇasambandhastasyākriyatvāt kriyāsambadhitvātkārakāṇāmanyathā kārakatvakṣatiḥ syāt tasmātsatkāryamiti sthitam /
  duḥkhatrayābhibhavasādhanaṃ prakṛtipuruṣānyatājñānaṃ tadupayogitvāt vyaktavairūpyaṃ pratipādanīyam / tacca vyaktaṃ pṛthivyādi taccāvyaktātpradhānādvilakṣaṇam yata idaṃ sakāraṇakaṃ tata evānityaṃ parābhimatavināśasāmagryā tirobhavati / avyāpakaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ hi kāryaṃ vyāpnoti na tu kāryaṃ kāraṇam / sakriyaṃ ca buddhyādayaḥ pūrvapūrvopāttaṃ dehaṃ parityajanti dehāntaraṃ copādadate saiva teṣāṃ kriyā pṛthivyādīnāṃ kriyā pariṇāmarūpeṇa prasiddhaiva / pratipuruṣaṃ buddhyādibhedādanekam tathā ghaṭaśarīrādibhedena pṛthivyādyapyanekam / svakāraṇāśritam yadyapi buddhyādīnāṃ pradhānabhedābhāvāt nāśrayāśrayibhāvastathāpi kathañcit bhedavivakṣayāśrayāśrayibhāvo yatheha vane tilakāḥ / sāvayavamavayavāvayavisaṃyogasaṃyogibuddhipradhānayostu na saṃyogastādātmyāt nāpi sattvarajastamasāṃ saṃyogaḥ aprāptipūrvikā prāptiḥ saṃyogastadabhāvāt / nityameva paratantraṃ svakārye 'haṅkārākhye janayitavye prakṛtyā pūramapekṣate anyathā kṣīṇā satī nāhaṅkāraṃ janayituṃ kṣamā bhavati tathāhaṅkāro 'pi svakārye prakṛtyā pūramapekṣate evaṃ kāraṇamātraṃ svakārye janayitavye tadapekṣāṃ kurute tathā ca svakārye janayitavye paratantraṃ vyaktam / yata ityabhivyāpya yaduktaṃ tadviparītamavyaktam yadyapyavyaktasya pariṇāmalakṣaṇākriyāsti tathāpi na parispandaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Even for a single fire, the capacity for manifold functions is seen through the distinction of burning and cooking; yet fire does not on that account become multiple. Just as individual blades of grass, though each is incapable of warding off heat, rain, and the like, when gathered together and having attained a particular configuration, those very [blades] become capable of warding off [heat and rain] — so too, a single thread, though incapable of the function of serving as a covering, those very [threads] when gathered together, having attained a particular configuration and having manifested the state of cloth, will perform the function of covering and the like. Therefore, the effect indeed pre-exists in the cause; its [so-called] production is merely its manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>). Objection: Is manifestation, prior to the operation of the cause, existent or non-existent? In the first case, the operation of the cause would be impossible, for when the existent arises, causes are not employed by anyone. In the second case, it follows that something non-existent is produced. Reply: No, for you too [face this]: what is this 'arising' — existent or non-existent? In the first case, we see no purpose for the cause. In the second case, if non-existent arising arises, then for that arising another arising [is needed], and for that yet another — there is a clear infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>). If arising is not different from the cloth itself, then when one says 'cloth,' one need not again say 'it arises,' due to redundancy. Likewise, having said 'it arises,' one need not again say 'cloth,' due to the very defect stated above. Nor can one say 'the cloth perishes,' due to contradiction. Therefore, the arising of the cloth is either the inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) of its own existence or the inherence with its own cause; and since inherence is eternal, in no way is the arising of the cloth possible [for you], nor are causes employed for that purpose. And thus, since the dependence on causes is for the manifestation of the already-existing cloth and the like, there is no fault. Nor is there a connection of the cause in the form of the cloth-effect, since [the latent effect] is without activity; since <s>kārakas</s> (grammatical agents of action) are connected with action, otherwise their nature as agents would be destroyed. Therefore, it is established that the effect pre-exists [in the cause] (<s>satkāryavāda</s>).
The knowledge of the difference between <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness) is the means for overcoming the three kinds of suffering (<s>duḥkhatraya</s>). Since it is useful for that [purpose], the dissimilarity of the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) should be explained. That manifest [reality] is earth and the like. And it has characteristics different from the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), i.e., <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primordial Matter). Because this [manifest] has a cause, it is therefore impermanent — it disappears by means of the aggregate of causes of destruction acknowledged by others. And non-pervasive — for the cause pervades the effect, but the effect does not pervade the cause. And possessed of activity — <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and the others abandon each previously assumed body and take up another body; that itself is their activity. The activity of earth and the like is well-known in the form of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). Multiple — due to the difference of <s>buddhi</s> and the like in each individual person; likewise earth and the like is also multiple due to the difference of pots, bodies, and so forth. Dependent on its own cause — although, since there is no differentiation of <s>Pradhāna</s> for <s>buddhi</s> and the like, there is no relation of support and supported, yet in some sense, with the intention of [expressing] difference, there is a relation of support and supported, like <s>tilaka</s> trees in a forest. Having parts — conjoined with the conjunction of parts and wholes. But there is no conjunction between <s>buddhi</s> and <s>Pradhāna</s>, since they are identical [in essence]; nor is there conjunction of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> [with each other], since conjunction is contact preceded by non-contact, and there is no such [prior non-contact]. Always dependent on another — when producing its own effect called <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle), [<s>buddhi</s>] depends on <s>Prakṛti</s> for completion; otherwise, being exhausted, it would not be capable of producing <s>ahaṅkāra</s>. Similarly, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> too depends on <s>Prakṛti</s> for completion in [producing] its own effect. Thus every cause, when producing its own effect, has such dependence. And thus the manifest, when producing its own effect, is dependent on another. That which is opposite to what has been stated by way of pervading [the characteristics of the manifest] — that is the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>). Although the unmanifest possesses activity in the form of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>), yet there is no vibration [or locomotion].

body.text: idānīṃ vyaktāvyaktayoḥ sādharmyaṃ puruṣācca vaidharmyaṃ pratipādanīyam / vyaktaṃ hi triguṇaṃ trayo guṇāḥ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakā asyeti / atra kāryakāraṇayorabhedāt sukhādiśabdaiḥ sattvādayo 'bhidhīyante triguṇamityuktyā sattvādīnāmātmaguṇatvaṃ parābhimatamapākṛtaṃ veditavyam / tathā aviveki yathā pradhānaṃ sato na vivicyate tathā mahadādayo 'pi pradhānānna vivicyante tatsvarūpatvāt / yadvā saṃbhūyakāritā 'vivekaḥ nahyekaṃ kiñcitkāryaṃ janayituṃ kṣamaṃ bhavatyapi tu saṃbhūya sarvaḥ sarvaṃ karoti / evamacetanaṃ pradhānabuddhyādayaḥ sarve acetanā tathā prasavarūpadharmavantaḥ / ete vyaktadharmāḥ kathitāsta evāvyaktasyāpītyavagantavyamidameva vyaktāvyaktayoḥ sādharmyam //
body.translated_text: Now the commonality (<s>sādharmya</s>) between the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) and the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), and the difference (<s>vaidharmya</s>) from <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness), are to be established. The manifest is indeed endowed with three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities)—the three <s>guṇas</s>, whose nature is pleasure, pain, and delusion, belong to it. Here, due to the non-difference of cause and effect, by the terms 'pleasure' and the like, <s>sattva</s> and the others are denoted. By the statement 'endowed with three guṇas,' it should be understood that the view held by others—that <s>sattva</s> and the rest are qualities of the self—is refuted. Likewise, 'non-discriminating' (<s>aviveki</s>): just as <s>Pradhāna</s> (the primal substance) is not distinguished from Being (<s>sat</s>), so too <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle) and the rest are not distinguished from <s>Pradhāna</s>, since they are of its very nature. Alternatively, 'non-discrimination' means 'operating in combination' (<s>saṃbhūyakāritā</s>), for no single [guṇa] alone is capable of producing any effect; rather, all [three] together produce everything. Likewise, 'non-conscious' (<s>acetana</s>): <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), and all the rest are non-conscious. And likewise, they possess the property of being productive (<s>prasavarūpa</s>). These properties of the manifest have been stated; they should be understood as belonging to the unmanifest as well—this is the very commonality between the manifest and the unmanifest.

body.text: ete sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ vyaktāvyakte nirūpite tadubhayagatadharmarahitatvāt viparītaḥ puruṣa iti puruṣasya vyaktāvyaktavaidharmyam / nanvahetumattvanityatvādi pradhānasādharmyaṃ puruṣasya pratīyate tathā cānekatvaṃ vyaktasādharmyamevaṃ sati kathaṃ vyaktāvyaktaviparītaḥ puruṣa iti cenna ahetumattvādisādharmye 'pyatraiguṇyādyasyāstyeva vaidharmyamiti na doṣaḥ / na ca traiguṇyamaprasiddham prītyaprītiviṣādātmakā guṇā iti sāṃkhyācāryāḥ / atra krameṇa prītiḥ sukhaṃ tadeva sattvam tathā aprītirduḥkhamaprītyātmako rajo guṇaḥ evaṃ viṣādo moho viṣādātmakastamoguṇaḥ / yanmate prītirduḥkhābhāvaḥ tathā duḥkhamapi prītyabhāvastannivṛttyarthaṃ mūlakāreṇātmagrahaṇaṃ kṛtamātmaśabdasya bhāvatattvena netaretarāśrayastathāsatyekasyāpi siddhirna syāt / prakāśapravṛttiniyamanameṣāṃ krameṇa prayojanamapyavagantavyam / kriyātmakena rajasa laghu sattvaṃ sarvatra nītaṃ syādativāyunā tūlāvayavavadyadi guruṇā tamasā niyamanaṃ na syāttamoniyataṃ tu kvacideva pravartayati tatastamo niyamārtham / anyonyābhibhavavṛttayaḥ / eteṣāmanyatamenārthavaśādudbhūtenānyatamamabhibhūyate tadyathā sattvaṃ rajastamasī abhibhūyātmanaḥ śāntāṃ vṛttimadhigacchati tathā rajaḥ sattvatamasī abhibhūya ghorāṃ vṛttimeti evaṃ tamaḥ sattvarajasī abhibhūya mūḍhāmiti / tathā 'nyonyāśrayavṛttayaḥ / yathāhuḥ sattvaṃ pravṛttiniyamāvāśritya rajastamasoḥ prakāśenopakaroti rajaḥ prakāśaniyamāvāśritya pravṛtyetarayoḥ tamaḥ prakāśapravṛttī āśritya niyamenetarayoriti / tathā anyonyajananavṛttayaḥ / anyatamo 'nyatamaṃ janayati jananamatra parimāṇaḥ sa ca guṇānāṃ sadṛśarūpaḥ / ata eva na hetumattvaṃ tattvāntarasya hetorabhāvāt / nāpyanityatvaṃ tattvāntare layābhāvāt / anyonyasaṃjñāvyabhicāriṇaśca / uktañca

children.translated_text: All are paired with one another; all pervade everywhere.

children.text: rajaso mithunaṃ sattvaṃ sattvasya mithunaṃ rajaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is paired with <s>rajas</s>; <s>rajas</s> is paired with <s>sattva</s>.

body.translated_text: Having thus determined the manifest and the unmanifest through commonality and difference, <s>Puruṣa</s> is the opposite, because it lacks the properties belonging to both—this is the difference of <s>Puruṣa</s> from the manifest and the unmanifest. [Objection:] But it is observed that <s>Puruṣa</s> has commonality with <s>Pradhāna</s> in being uncaused, eternal, and so forth; and likewise, plurality is a commonality with the manifest. This being so, how can <s>Puruṣa</s> be the opposite of the manifest and unmanifest? [Reply:] No, this is not a fault, because even though there is commonality in being uncaused and so forth, there is indeed a difference such as the absence of the three <s>guṇas</s>. And the three <s>guṇas</s> are not unestablished—the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> masters [define them]: the <s>guṇas</s> are of the nature of delight (<s>prīti</s>), displeasure (<s>aprīti</s>), and dejection (<s>viṣāda</s>). Here, in order: delight is pleasure, and that is <s>sattva</s>; likewise displeasure is pain, and the <s>guṇa</s> <s>rajas</s> is of the nature of displeasure; similarly dejection is delusion, and the <s>guṇa</s> <s>tamas</s> is of the nature of dejection. To refute the view that delight is the mere absence of pain, and likewise pain is the mere absence of delight, the root author used the term 'nature' (<s>ātma</s>), [indicating that each has] real positive existence, so there is no mutual dependence—otherwise even one [guṇa] would not be established. The purpose of these [guṇas] should also be understood as, respectively, illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>), activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), and restraint (<s>niyamana</s>). By <s>rajas</s>, whose nature is activity, the light <s>sattva</s> would be carried everywhere—like a cotton filament by an excessive wind—were it not restrained by the heavy <s>tamas</s>. But [sattva], restrained by <s>tamas</s>, operates only in certain places; hence <s>tamas</s> serves the purpose of restraint. Their modes of operation are through mutual suppression (<s>anyonyābhibhava</s>): when any one of them predominates due to circumstances, it suppresses the other—for example, <s>sattva</s> suppresses <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> and attains its peaceful mode; likewise <s>rajas</s> suppresses <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> and enters its agitated mode; similarly <s>tamas</s> suppresses <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> and [enters] its deluded [mode]. Likewise, their modes of operation are through mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>): as it is said—<s>sattva</s>, depending on activity and restraint, assists <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> through illumination; <s>rajas</s>, depending on illumination and restraint, [assists] the others through activity; <s>tamas</s>, depending on illumination and activity, [assists] the others through restraint. Likewise, their modes of operation are through mutual generation (<s>anyonyajanana</s>): one generates another. 'Generation' here means [change of] proportion, and this [proportion] is of the same nature as the <s>guṇas</s>. For this very reason, there is no 'being caused' [in the sense of arising from something else], since there is no cause that is a different principle; nor is there impermanence, since there is no dissolution into a different principle. And they are inseparable in their designations. As it is said:

children.translated_text: And of <s>tamas</s>, the two pairs are <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>.
The state of being paired means the invariable co-occurrence.

children.translated_text: From the fixed determination of birth, death, and the instruments [of knowledge],
and from their non-simultaneous activity, the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established, and also from the contrariety of the three <s>guṇas</s>.

body.translated_text: The union of both <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> is called <s>tamas</s>. / Neither a beginning of their conjunction nor their disjunction is perceived. // Thus. But their fixed function is this: lightness and the capacity to illuminate belong to <s>sattva</s> alone, not to either of the other two. Therein, the quality of lightness, which is the cause of upward movement, coexists with the absence of heaviness — by which fire has an upward-flaming movement. That same [quality] is the cause of lateral movement in some cases, as with wind. Thus, lightness is the cause of the instruments' skill in functioning; in heaviness, however, they would be sluggish. Thus the illuminating nature of <s>sattva</s> has been stated. <s>Sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>, being inactive, sink in producing their own effects and are supported by <s>rajas</s>. Being freed from sluggishness, one becomes energetic and exerts effort. And it has been said: '<s>Sattva</s> is light and illuminating; desired. <s>Rajas</s> is stimulating and mobile.' Why is it stimulating? Because it is mobile. <s>Rajas</s>, by its mobility, would set in motion the three-fold quality everywhere, if there were no obstruction from <s>tamas</s>, which is heavy and covering. But by <s>tamas</s>, activity is turned away here and there and set in motion only somewhere — thus <s>tamas</s> is the regulator. As they say: '<s>Tamas</s> is indeed heavy and covering.' Accordingly, <s>sattva</s> alone is light and illuminating; <s>rajas</s> alone is stimulating and mobile; <s>tamas</s> alone is heavy and covering. Now, if it be objected that <s>guṇas</s> whose nature is mutual opposition should, by the logic of <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>, merely obstruct each other rather than cooperate in producing a single effect — this is not so, because the cooperation of even such entities in producing a single effect is demonstrated. For example, oil is opposed to fire, yet combined with fire it produces the effect characterized as the illumination of forms. And just as <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), though mutually opposed in nature, when combined produce the effect of sustaining the body — so too <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, though of opposed nature, will coexist together and will cooperate in producing a single effect, in accordance with the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>. And it has been said: 'Their functioning is purposeful, like a lamp.' Since the <s>guṇas</s> are of the nature of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), even in unity there is diversity in the form of the dominated and the dominating. It has been said: 'One and the same woman, endowed with good qualities, family, beauty, character, and youth, brings pleasure to her husband. What is the reason? Because pleasure arises from her with respect to him. That very same woman brings pain to her co-wives. What is the reason? Because pain arises from her with respect to them. Likewise, that very same woman deludes another man who cannot obtain her. What is the reason? Because delusion arises from her with respect to him.' By this analogy of the woman, all entities are explained. Therein, that which is the cause of pleasure is <s>sattva</s>, whose nature is pleasure. Likewise, that which is the cause of pain is <s>rajas</s>, whose nature is pain. And that which is the cause of delusion is <s>tamas</s>, whose nature is delusion. Therefore, from the operation of the cause, the effect exists prior [to its manifestation]. That very effect again manifests through the operation of that cause — just as the tortoise's limbs, which already exist, emerge and are distinguished: 'This is the tortoise's body; these are its limbs.' When those are retracted, they become unmanifest within it. Similarly, pots, earrings, and the like, which already exist in clay, gold, and the like, manifest and are distinguished: 'This is the clay; this pot is its effect,' and so on. Likewise, earth and the other [gross elements], which already exist, manifest from their cause, the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), and are distinguished: 'This is its cause; this is its effect.' Similarly, the <s>tanmātras</s>, which already exist, manifest from <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) and are distinguished. Likewise, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, which already exists, comes into manifestation from <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle); and <s>Mahat</s>, which already exists, comes into manifestation from <s>Mūlaprakṛti</s> (Root Nature). Thus the differentiation of the manifest world, which is an effect, arises directly and successively from the supreme Unmanifest, which is its cause. At the time of dissolution alone, pots, earrings, and the like, entering the lump of clay or the mass of gold, become unmanifest — though manifest in the form of the cause, they become unmanifest in the form of the effect. Similarly, earth and the other elements, entering the <s>tanmātras</s>, make the <s>tanmātras</s> manifest in their own form — though the cause is manifest in its own form, it does not manifest its own particular effect-form within itself. The <s>tanmātras</s> likewise enter <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and make <s>ahaṅkāra</s> unmanifest relative to themselves. So too <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, entering <s>Mahat</s>, makes <s>Mahat</s> unmanifest; and <s>Mahat</s>, entering <s>Pradhāna</s>, its own cause, makes it unmanifest. But <s>Pradhāna</s> does not enter anywhere, because it is uncaused; yet it is the unmanifest cause of all effects. Thus there is non-differentiation. In <s>Prakṛti</s>, differentiation and non-differentiation of the universe [occur] in this way. Some, taking the Unmanifest, or <s>Mahat</s>, or <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, or the sense-organs, or the elements as the self, worship those very things. But they are to be refuted in the manner to be stated. <s>Puruṣa</s> exists as distinct from the Unmanifest and the rest. The Unmanifest, <s>Mahat</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and the rest serve another's purpose. Why? Because they are composites. Whatever is a composite is seen to serve another's purpose — like oil, betel, ghee, curd, milk, food, clothing, and the like. All composites partake of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion. And that for whose sake the composites exist — that is <s>Puruṣa</s>. Now, if it be objected: 'A bed, seat, and the like are composites, and the composite body and the like are seen to serve another composite, not the self; therefore they should establish only another composite, not an uncomposite self' — this is not correct. For if a composite served only another composite, then that other composite too, being composite, would serve yet another composite, and that one too, being composite, would likewise serve another — and so on, resulting in an insuperable infinite regress. Moreover, the pervasion is only with serving-another and composite-nature, not with composite-nature and serving-another. Nor should it be said that it is imagined so merely because it is seen in examples. For if one who wishes to establish through inference, in the subject of proof, properties seen only in examples — then because of the absence in mountains and the like of kitchen-nature and the like found in the example of a kitchen, all inference would be destroyed. As they say: properties such as being composed of three <s>guṇas</s> are pervaded by composite-nature; and when these are excluded from this other [i.e., <s>Puruṣa</s>], they exclude the three-<s>guṇa</s> nature [from him] — just as when brahmin-hood departs, so does the Kaṭha-identity and the like. From superintendence too, the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s> is established — because <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and the rest, which are of the nature of the three <s>guṇas</s>, are superintended, just as a chariot and the like are superintended by a driver and the like. So too <s>buddhi</s> and the rest, whose nature is pleasure, pain, and delusion, must be superintended by another. From the fact of enjoyership too, the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s> should be ascertained. For pleasure and pain, the objects of enjoyment — experienced as agreeable and disagreeable respectively — are experienced by each individual self. Therefore, there must be some experiencer of these in their agreeable and disagreeable aspects. Nor should it be said that <s>buddhi</s> and the rest themselves serve this function, for since they are of the nature of pleasure and the like, their self-cognition would involve the fallacy of self-dependence (<s>ātmāśraya</s>). From the activity directed toward liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) too, the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s> is established. <s>Kaivalya</s> (isolation), characterized by the absolute cessation of the triple suffering, does not belong to <s>buddhi</s> and the rest, for they are of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion — how could they be separated from their own nature? Therefore, since the activity of scriptures and great minds is directed toward liberation, there exists a self distinct from <s>buddhi</s> and the rest — thus the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s> is established. Now, even if the existence of a self distinct from <s>buddhi</s> and the rest be granted, is it one for each body, or is there only one [universal self]? We say: it is indeed distinct [for each body], because the regulation of birth, death, and the rest would otherwise be inexplicable, and plurality alone is possible. And it has been said by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers:

jātiviśiṣṭābhirapūrvābhirdehendriyamano 'haṅkārabuddhivedanābhiḥ puruṣasyābhisambandho janma na tu puruṣasya pariṇāmastasyāpariṇāmitvāt teṣāmeva ca dehādīnāmupāttānāṃ parityāgo maraṇaṃ na tvātmano vināśastasya kūṭasthasya nityatvāt / buddhyādīni karaṇāni trayodaśa teṣāṃ janmamaraṇakaraṇānāṃ pratiniyamo vyavasthā sā tviyaṃ śarvaśarīreṣvekasminpuruṣe na sambhavati tathā satyekasminsukhini sarve sukhinaḥ syuḥ duḥkhini vā duḥkhino bhaveyuḥ tathā ekasmin mriyamāṇe sarve mriyeran jāyamāne ca jāyeran evamekasminnandhabadhirādau sarva eva tathā syuḥ na tvevamasti tathā ekasminvicitte sarve vicittāḥ syurityavyavasthā puruṣabhede tu samyagupapadyate vyavasthā / nacaikasminnapi puruṣe dehāntaropādhivaśāt upapadyata eva vyavastheti vācyam karacaraṇastanādibhedenāpi janmamaraṇādivyavasthā syāt / guṇatrayaviparyayādapi puruṣabahutvamavaseyam / tadyathā kecitsattvabahulāḥ yathorddhvasrotasaḥ kecidrahobahulāḥ yathā manuṣyāḥ kecittamobahulāḥ yathā tiryagyonayaḥ /

  pradhānapuruṣayoḥ saṃyogakṛto 'yaṃ sargaḥ sa cāpekṣāṃ vinā bhinnayorna sambhavati apekṣā ca svadarśanārthaṃ puruṣeṇa pradhānasya pradhānaṃ hi viṣayātmakatayā bhogyam bhogaśca bhoktāramantareṇa na bhavatīti bhoktrapekṣā pradhānasya puruṣasya svakaivalyārthaṃ pradhānāpekṣā pradhānena hi bhogyena sambhinnaḥ puruṣastadgataṃ duḥkhatrayaṃ svātmanyabhimanyamānaḥ kaivalyaṃ prārthayate tattu sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātikāraṇakaṃ sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātiśca pradhānamantarā na bhavatīti puruṣasya pradhānāpekṣayā paṅgvandhavadubhayoḥ saṃyogaḥ bhogāyānādiparamparāsaṃyukto 'pi kaivalyāya punaḥ saṃyujyate sa ca saṃyogo mahadādisargamantareṇa bhogāpavargayoḥ samartho na bhavatīti saṃyoga eva mahadādisargaṃ karoti / uktañca /

children.translated_text: From <s>Prakṛti</s> [arises] <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle), from that <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), from that the group of sixteen,
and from five of that group of sixteen [arise] the five gross elements (<s>bhūtas</s>).

body.translated_text:
The association of <s>Puruṣa</s> with body, sense organs, mind (<s>manas</s>), ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), and sensations — each of a specific kind, each unprecedented — constitutes birth; but it is not a transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) of <s>Puruṣa</s>, since <s>Puruṣa</s> is not subject to transformation. And the relinquishment of those very assumed bodies and other [principles] is death; but it is not the destruction of the self (<s>ātman</s>), since the self is immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>) and eternal. The <s>karaṇas</s> (instruments) are the thirteen [principles] beginning with <s>buddhi</s>. The fixed determination (<s>pratiniyama</s>) — that is, the orderly arrangement — of birth, death, and the instruments does not occur if there is a single <s>Puruṣa</s> for all bodies. For if that were so, when one is happy, all would be happy; or when one suffers, all would suffer. Likewise, when one dies, all would die, and when one is born, all would be born. Similarly, when one is blind or deaf, all would be so as well. But this is not the case. Likewise, when one is variegated in mental disposition, all would be variegated — [resulting in] the absence of orderly arrangement. But when <s>Puruṣas</s> are different, the orderly arrangement is properly established. Nor should it be argued that even for a single <s>Puruṣa</s>, the orderly arrangement is established due to the conditioning of different bodies — for then the orderly arrangement of birth, death, and so forth would apply even to [different parts of the same body such as] hands, feet, breasts, and so on. The plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> should also be inferred from the contrariety of the three <s>guṇas</s>: some beings are predominantly <s>sāttvika</s> (luminous), such as the upward-flowing beings (gods); some are predominantly <s>rājasika</s> (active), such as humans; some are predominantly <s>tāmasika</s> (inert), such as those born in animal wombs.
Just as the plurality of <s>Puruṣa</s> [has been established], so too should be understood its being devoid of the three <s>guṇas</s>, its nature as discriminative consciousness (<s>vivekitva</s>), its being not an object (<s>aviṣayatva</s>), its being uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇatva</s>), its being sentient (<s>cetanatva</s>), its being non-productive (<s>aprasavadharmin</s>), its being a witness (<s>sākṣitva</s>), and other [properties].
This creation (<s>sarga</s>) is produced by the conjunction of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s>; and that [creation], without mutual need (<s>apekṣā</s>), is not possible for [two principles] that are separate. The need is as follows: <s>Puruṣa</s> needs <s>Pradhāna</s> for the purpose of self-knowledge, for <s>Pradhāna</s>, being of the nature of objects, is to be experienced (<s>bhogya</s>), and experience does not occur without an experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) — thus <s>Pradhāna</s> needs an experiencer. <s>Puruṣa</s> needs <s>Pradhāna</s> for the purpose of its own liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>), for <s>Puruṣa</s>, conjoined with <s>Pradhāna</s> (the object of experience), falsely attributes the threefold suffering contained in it to itself, and thus desires <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation). But that [kaivalya] is caused by the discriminative knowledge of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>sattvapuruṣānyatākhyāti</s>), and that discriminative knowledge does not occur without <s>Pradhāna</s> — thus <s>Puruṣa</s> needs <s>Pradhāna</s>. Like a lame man and a blind man, the conjunction of both serves experience (<s>bhoga</s>); though conjoined from beginningless successive [births] for experience, [<s>Puruṣa</s>] conjoins again for <s>kaivalya</s>. And that conjunction, without the creation of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest, is not capable of [accomplishing] experience and liberation — therefore the conjunction itself produces the creation of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest. As it is said:

The eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements)—this group numbering sixteen is the 'set of sixteen.' And it is said: from the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> (sound-subtle element), space (<s>ākāśa</s>) arises, possessing the quality of sound; from the <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s> (touch-subtle element) combined with the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s>, wind (<s>vāyu</s>) arises, possessing the qualities of sound and touch; from the <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s> (form-subtle element) combined with the <s>śabda</s>- and <s>sparśa-tanmātras</s>, fire (<s>tejas</s>) arises, possessing the qualities of sound, touch, and form; from the <s>rasa-tanmātra</s> (taste-subtle element) combined with the <s>śabda</s>-, <s>sparśa</s>-, and <s>rūpa-tanmātras</s>, water (<s>jala</s>) arises, possessing the qualities of sound, touch, form, and taste; from the <s>gandha-tanmātra</s> (smell-subtle element) combined with the <s>śabda</s>-, <s>sparśa</s>-, <s>rūpa</s>-, and <s>rasa-tanmātras</s>, earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) arises, possessing the qualities of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell.
Ascertainment (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect); the designation is used without distinction between the active and non-active [forms]. <s>Dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>virāga</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty)—these are the <s>sāttvika</s> properties of <s>buddhi</s>; their opposites—<s>adharma</s> (non-virtue) and the rest—are <s>tāmasa</s>. From the property of <s>buddhi</s> called <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), the manifestation of <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the other [powers] occurs. And these are:
<s>Aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>mahimā</s> (greatness), <s>garimā</s> (heaviness), <s>laghimā</s> (lightness),
<s>prāpti</s> (obtainment), <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will), <s>īśitva</s> (lordship), and <s>vaśitva</s> (mastery)—these are the eight <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers).
[Objection:] But the group of sense organs, which is the 'set of eleven,' and the five <s>tanmātras</s>—these two kinds of creation proceed from <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense). How then, from a single <s>ahaṅkāra</s> as cause, can the creation be of dissimilar nature, being of illuminating and inert character? [Reply:] What was said is not sound—the group of eleven sense organs arises from the <s>sāttvika</s> (illuminating) <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, due to [its] illumination and lightness; while from the <s>tāmasa</s> (inert) <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, called <s>bhūtādi</s> (source of elements), arises the group of <s>tanmātras</s>. Even though <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is one, through the predominance and suppression of the <s>guṇas</s>, it produces different effects. [Objection:] If creation is through <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> alone, then what is the use of <s>rajas</s>, which accomplishes nothing? [Reply:] No—because the root author [says] 'from the <s>taijasa</s> (rajasic), both'—from the <s>taijasa ahaṅkāra</s>, both groups arise, that is, the two types of creation belong to <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> [but are activated by rajas]. Even though <s>rajas</s> has no separate product, still <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>, though inherently capable, do not produce their effects by themselves without being activated; when activated by <s>rajas</s>, they become empowered through its grace and become capable of producing their respective effects—hence 'from the rajasic, both.' As they say: in both products, <s>rajas</s> has causality through being the door to the arising of the activity of <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>; thus <s>rajas</s> is not useless.
The discussion of the <s>indriyas</s> has been done in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, so out of fear of prolixity, it is not elaborated here. <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle), <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> (mind) are the inner organs (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>). They have their own defining characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>)—that is, each has its own unique characteristic: for <s>Mahat</s>, it is ascertainment (<s>adhyavasāya</s>); for <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, self-conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>); and for <s>manas</s>, its function is volition (<s>saṅkalpa</s>). The twofold nature of their function is stated through common and uncommon [aspects]: 'this [uncommon function] is non-common.' This stated uncommon function is [what has been described]; while the common function of the organs is the five breaths (<s>prāṇa</s>) beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>—the five <s>vāyus</s> (vital airs) are the function of the three [inner] organs; [they are called] 'life' (<s>jīvana</s>), since in their presence there is existence and in their absence, non-existence. Among these: <s>prāṇa</s> operates at the tip of the nose, the heart, the navel, and the big toe; <s>apāna</s> operates at the nape, back, sides, anus, and genitals; <s>samāna</s> operates at the heart, navel, and all joints; <s>udāna</s> operates at the heart, throat, palate, crown of the head, and the point between the eyebrows; <s>vyāna</s> operates in the skin—these are the five <s>vāyus</s>.
Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is fivefold; as it is said: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life)—these, respectively designated as <s>tamas</s> (darkness), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom), and <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness), constitute the five divisions.
The intellectual creation (<s>pratyayasarga</s>) and its divisions—though they exist, they are not demonstrated here out of fear of excessive length. The intellectual creation is the creation of <s>buddhi</s>. As it is said: 'This intellectual creation is called error (<s>viparyaya</s>), incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>), contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), and accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>).' <s>Pratyaya</s> means <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), since 'by this one cognizes'; its creation is the <s>pratyayasarga</s>. The divine creation (<s>daivasarga</s>), however, has been clearly explained by the root author himself: this divine creation is of eight kinds—<s>Brāhma</s> (pertaining to <s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Prājāpatya</s> (pertaining to <s>Prajāpati</s>), <s>Aindra</s> (pertaining to <s>Indra</s>), <s>Paitrya</s> (pertaining to the <s>Pitṛs</s>), <s>Gāndharva</s> (pertaining to <s>Gandharvas</s>), <s>Yākṣa</s> (pertaining to <s>Yakṣas</s>), <s>Rākṣasa</s> (pertaining to <s>Rākṣasas</s>), and <s>Paiśāca</s> (pertaining to <s>Piśācas</s>)—thus the divine creation is of eight kinds. Animal births (<s>tiryagyoni</s>) are of five kinds: domestic animals, wild animals, birds, reptiles, and immovable beings. And human creation is of one kind—disregarding the distinctions of caste such as <s>brāhmaṇa</s> status and the like, since the bodily form is not different among the four [castes].

nanu prādhāniko 'yaṃ sargaḥ pradhānaṃ ca jaḍaṃ kathaṃ svārthaṃ parārthaṃ vā pravṛttiṃ kartumarhati tasmātkenaciccetanena prakṛtyadhiṣṭhātrā bhavitavyam / na ca kṣetrajñāstathā teṣāṃ prakṛtisvarūpānabhijñatvāt tasmādasti prakṛteradhiṣṭhātā kaścitsarvajñaḥ sa eveśvara iti cenna acetanamapi prayojanavaśāt pravartamānaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā vatsavivṛddhyarthamacetanamapi kṣīraṃ pravartate tathā jaḍāpi prakṛtiḥ puruṣavimokṣāya pravartiṣyate / kiñcābhokturīśvarasya pravṛttau na karuṇāṃ vinā 'nyat prayojanaṃ paśyāmaḥ / sā ca nirupādhiparaduḥkhaprahāṇecchā sṛṣṭeḥ pūrvaṃ prāṇyabhāvādeva tatsambandhiduḥkhābhāvāt kasya nivṛttau pravṛttiḥ syādīśvarasya / na ca sargānantaramīśvarapravṛttiḥ sargasya jātatvādeva neśvaraprayojanaṃ paśyāmaḥ / na ca duḥkhanivṛttiḥ prayojanaṃ tadarthaṃ tatpravṛttau jagati ko 'pi duḥkhī na syāt / uktañca prekṣāvataḥ pravṛtteḥ svārthakāruṇyābhyāṃ vyāptatvāt te ca jagatsargādvyāvartamāne prekṣāvatpravṛttipūrvakatvamapi nivartayataḥ na hyāptasakalepsitasya bhagavato jagatsṛjataḥ kimapyabhilaṣitaṃ bhavati nāpi kāruṇyādasya sarge pravṛttiḥ prāksargājjīvānāmindriyaśarīraviṣayānutpattau duḥkhābhāvena kasya prahāṇecchā kāruṇyena sṛṣṭiḥ sṛṣṭyā ca kāruṇyamiti parasparāśrayaḥ / api ca karuṇayā pravṛttaḥ sukhina eva jantūnsṛjet na daridrān / na ca karmavaicitryāt jagadvaicitryam tarhi kṛtamīśvareṇa tata eva jagadvaicitryopapatteḥ pravṛttistu pārārthyaprayojanavaśāt jaḍasyāpi dṛśyate vatsavivṛddhinimittaṃ dugdhasyeva /
  nanu bhavatu prakṛteḥ pravartakaḥ puruṣārtho nivartakaṃ na tu kamapi paśyāma iti cenna yathā nartakī pariṣadbhyo nṛtyaṃ darśayitvā svayameva nivartate na tu tasyāḥ svanivṛttau nivartakāntarāpekṣā tathā śabdādyātmakaṃ svasvarūpaṃ puruṣādbhedena prakāśya sādhitapuruṣaprayojanā svayameva nivartate prakṛtiḥ / yathāhuḥ sāṃkhyācāryāḥ /

children.text: raṅgasya darśayitvā nivartate yathā nartakī nṛtyāt /
children.translated_text: Just as a dancer, having displayed [her art] to the audience, withdraws from the dance,
so <s>Prakṛti</s>, having revealed herself to <s>Puruṣa</s>, withdraws.

body.translated_text: Now, if it be objected: 'This creation belongs to <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), and <s>Pradhāna</s> is insentient — how can it undertake activity for its own purpose or for another's? Therefore, there must be some conscious superintendent of <s>Prakṛti</s>. And the individual souls (<s>kṣetrajñas</s>) are not such, because they are ignorant of the true nature of <s>Prakṛti</s>. Therefore, there exists some omniscient superintendent of <s>Prakṛti</s> — that is <s>Īśvara</s> (God).' To this we say: No. Even the insentient is seen to act under the compulsion of purpose — just as milk, though insentient, flows for the nourishment of the calf, so too <s>Prakṛti</s>, though inert, will act for the liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>. Moreover, in the activity of <s>Īśvara</s>, who is not an experiencer, we see no motive other than compassion. And that compassion — defined as the unconditioned desire to remove others' suffering — before creation, since there are no living beings, and hence no suffering belonging to them, for whose cessation would <s>Īśvara</s> act? Nor can <s>Īśvara's</s> activity follow after creation, since creation has already occurred, and we see no purpose for <s>Īśvara</s>. Nor is the cessation of suffering the motive, for if he acted for that purpose, no one in the world would suffer. And it has been said: since the activity of an intelligent agent is pervaded by self-interest and compassion, and since these two are excluded from the creation of the world, they exclude even the fact that it is preceded by intelligent agency. For the Blessed One who has attained all desires has no wish whatsoever in creating the world. Nor does he act in creation out of compassion, for before creation, when sense-organs, bodies, and objects of living beings have not yet arisen, there being no suffering, for whose removal would compassion motivate creation? Compassion requires creation, and creation requires compassion — this is mutual dependence. Furthermore, if motivated by compassion, he should create only happy beings, not wretched ones. Nor should it be said that the variety of the world is due to the variety of <s>karma</s>, for then <s>Īśvara</s> has accomplished nothing, since the variety of the world is already explained by that [<s>karma</s>] alone. But activity is seen even in the inert when motivated by the purpose of serving another — like milk for the nourishment of the calf. Now, if it be objected: 'Let it be granted that <s>Puruṣa's</s> purpose motivates <s>Prakṛti</s>, but we see no cause for its cessation' — to this we say: No. Just as a dancer, having displayed her dance to the audience, ceases of her own accord — no separate agent is needed for her cessation — so too <s>Prakṛti</s>, having revealed her own nature consisting of sound and the rest as distinct from <s>Puruṣa</s>, having accomplished the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, ceases of her own accord. As the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers say:

body.text: nanu yathā darśitanṛtyā nartakī draṣṭṛkautuhalātpunaḥ pravartate tathā prakṛtirapi puruṣāyātmānaṃ darśayitvā nivṛttāpi punaścet pravartete tadā muktānāmapi punaḥ saṃsāraprāptiḥ syāditi cenna yathā parapuruṣadarśanāsahā sūryadarśanavarjitāpi kulavadhūḥ pramādādvigalitāṅgapaṭā cedavalokyate parapuruṣeṇa tadā 'sau tathā pravartate 'pramattāṃ yathaināṃ punaḥ puruṣāntarāni na paśyanti tathā prakṛtiḥ kulavadhūto 'pyadhikā dṛṣṭā biṃbakena punarna darśanamārgameti / uktaṃ ca /

children.text: prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ na kiñcidastīti me matirbhavati /
children.translated_text: Nothing is more modest than <s>Prakṛti</s> — this is my conviction,
who, [thinking] 'I have been seen,' never again comes into the sight of <s>Puruṣa</s>.

body.translated_text: Now, if it be objected: 'Just as a dancer who has displayed her dance performs again due to the audience's curiosity, so too, if <s>Prakṛti</s>, having displayed herself to <s>Puruṣa</s>, withdraws and then performs again, then even for the liberated there would be a return to <s>saṃsāra</s>' — to this we say: No. Just as a virtuous wife who cannot bear being seen by another man, even if she normally avoids the sight of the sun — if by accident her garment slips from her body and she is seen by another man, then she acts in such a way that, being vigilant, other men will never see her again — so too <s>Prakṛti</s>, being even more modest than the virtuous wife, having been seen [by <s>Puruṣa</s>] as a reflected image, never again enters the path of being seen. And it has been said:

body.text:
dharmo jñānaṃ virāga aiśvaryamiti sāttvikā buddhidharmāḥ /
  adharmājñānāvairāgyānaiśvaryābhidhānāścatvārastāmasāḥ /
atra jñānavarjitaiḥ saptabhiḥ prakṛtirbadhnātyātmānaṃ vivekakhyātyā prakṛtipuruṣānyatājñānena saiva vimocayati / uktañca /

children.translated_text: Thus, by seven forms, <s>Prakṛti</s> binds the self by herself;
and that very same [<s>Prakṛti</s>] liberates for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> by one form alone.

body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>virāga</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (mastery) — these are the <s>sāttvika</s> properties of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). <s>Adharma</s> (vice), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>avairāgya</s> (attachment), and <s>anaiśvarya</s> (powerlessness) — these four are the <s>tāmasa</s> properties. Of these, by the seven excluding knowledge, <s>Prakṛti</s> binds the self. By the knowledge of discrimination (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) — the knowledge of the otherness of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — that very same [<s>Prakṛti</s>] liberates. And it has been said:

children.text: yathā vidrumamaṇimauktikaśuktimakarakacchapanāgaśaṃkhakapardakādīn vihāya paramakāruṇikena līlāvigrahadhāriṇā bhagavatā ratnyānyeva samuddhṛtānyudadherdevasamṛddhyarthaṃ tathā jalpatarkābhāsākhyā 'nyatrasulabhaprameyavitaṇḍādīṃśca vihāya sāṃkhyamātaikalabhyaprameyaratnāni sāṃkhyataṃtrādhyayanapariśramālasānāṃ sāṃkhyatantrodadhermayā samuddhṛtāni /
children.translated_text: Just as the supremely compassionate Blessed One, who assumes a playful form, having set aside corals, gems, pearls, oysters, <s>makara</s> (sea-creatures), turtles, serpents, conches, cowries, and the like, extracted only the jewels from the ocean for the prosperity of the gods — so too, having set aside the fallacious reasoning (<s>jalpa</s>), semblance of inference (<s>tarkābhāsa</s>), and other easily obtainable topics such as refutation (<s>vitaṇḍā</s>) found elsewhere, I have extracted from the ocean of <s>Sāṅkhya</s> doctrine the jewels of proof (<s>prameya</s>) obtainable only through the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> system, for the sake of those who are weary from the labor of studying the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> treatise.
As long as the story of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [endures], as long as the moon and the sun [shine],
may this <s>Sāṅkhyatattvapradīpa</s> (Light on the Principles of Sāṅkhya) remain upon the earth.

body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Sāṅkhyatattvapradīpa</s>, illuminated by the <s>yati</s> (ascetic) <s>Kavirāja</s>, disciple of the revered <s>Śrī Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the worshipful <s>Paramahaṃsa Parivrājakācārya</s> (supreme wandering ascetic teacher), is complete.
